name: CA-50
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district (D+10 PVI) with incumbent Scott Peters running
Peters holds a large financial advantage ($2.6M on hand) with no outside opposition

model.rationale: Peters is a well-funded incumbent in a D+10 district, and markets price his reelection at roughly 95%, consistent with the fundamentals-based margin of about 21 points. With no polling or serious outside spending against him, there is little evidence to move off that baseline.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Peters or an unusually strong Republican midterm environment could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Scott Peters, the Democratic incumbent, is seeking another term in a San Diego-area district that leans Democratic by about ten points. He advanced to the general election and holds a substantial financial edge, with roughly $2.6 million on hand and no outside groups opposing him. His Republican opponent, Steve Cohen, has reported little visible fundraising activity.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and money. Prediction markets price Peters as a heavy favorite. The seat is expected to remain in Democratic hands by a wide margin, though the absence of polling leaves some room for uncertainty.
